l4_steps.name: Identify post-flight survey eligible pax
l4_steps.input: Flight departure confirmation and boarded pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Eligible passenger list with contact metadata
l4_steps.kpi: Eligible pax coverage ≥ 95% of boarded passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa passenger records may have missing or stale email addresses when bookings originate from OTA channels without email pass-through, reducing survey reach by up to 20%

l4_steps.name: Validate opt-in status and contact data
l4_steps.input: Eligible passenger list from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Suppression list (opted-out / invalid email) and validated send list
l4_steps.kpi: Suppression accuracy 100% — zero survey sends to opted-out contacts
l4_steps.pain_point: GDPR and CCPA compliance requires real-time suppression list sync between Altéa loyalty database and Salesforce Marketing Cloud; sync lag of >4 hours risks regulatory breach

l4_steps.name: Generate personalised survey link and dispatch
l4_steps.input: Validated send list with flight metadata (route, cabin class, flight number)
l4_steps.output: Personalised survey email sent within 24 hours of flight arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Survey dispatch latency ≤ 24 hours post-arrival; email deliverability ≥ 97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics dynamic survey personalisation requires clean flight-level metadata from Altéa; missing cabin class data causes generic survey routing, degrading response quality for premium cabin feedback

l4_steps.name: Monitor survey response rate by flight cohort
l4_steps.input: Dispatch log and response ingestion feed
l4_steps.output: Real-time response rate dashboard per flight/route
l4_steps.kpi: Target survey response rate ≥ 20%; industry benchmark ~15–18%
l4_steps.pain_point: Response rates on short-haul routes (<90 min) are structurally lower (8–12%) due to rapid passenger disengagement post-flight; blended NPS may over-index on long-haul sentiment

l4_steps.name: Send reminder to non-responders at 48 hours
l4_steps.input: Non-response flag from Qualtrics XM at 48-hour mark
l4_steps.output: Single reminder email dispatched to eligible non-responders
l4_steps.kpi: Reminder lift in response rate ≥ 5 percentage points; max 1 reminder per passenger
l4_steps.pain_point: Over-surveying risk: passengers who received a complaint follow-up (CX-05) or loyalty communication (CX-01) within the same 72-hour window must be suppressed from reminder sends to avoid fatigue and NPS score inflation

l4_steps.name: Validate response completeness and ingest to analytics
l4_steps.input: Raw survey responses from Qualtrics XM export
l4_steps.output: Cleaned response dataset loaded to AWS S3 data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Partial response exclusion rate ≤ 5% of total submissions; ingestion latency ≤ 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics partial completion records (pax abandoned mid-survey) can corrupt NPS scoring if included; no native auto-exclusion rule in Qualtrics XM without custom workflow configuration

l4_steps.name: Classify respondents as Promoter, Passive, or Detractor
l4_steps.input: Validated 0–10 NPS responses from AWS S3
l4_steps.output: Classified respondent list: Promoters (9–10), Passives (7–8), Detractors (0–6)
l4_steps.kpi: NPS score = (% Promoters − % Detractors); target airline industry NPS ≥ 40
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics NPS calculation runs at batch rather than real-time; daily NPS score may lag 12–18 hours behind actual flight completions during peak travel periods, delaying detractor recovery initiation

l4_steps.name: Perform text analytics on verbatim comments
l4_steps.input: Open-text survey responses classified by NPS segment
l4_steps.output: Themed sentiment clusters: e.g. boarding, crew, catering, IFE, baggage
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-classification accuracy ≥ 85% vs. manual coding sample; ≤ 10% uncategorised verbatims
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics Text iQ topic models require periodic retraining as language patterns evolve; stale models misclassify emerging complaint themes (e.g. NDC booking friction) into legacy categories, masking new failure drivers

l4_steps.name: Flag detractor responses and route to recovery queue
l4_steps.input: Detractor records (NPS 0–6) with verbatim themes from Qualtrics XM
l4_steps.output: Service cases created in Salesforce Service Cloud with priority tier based on score severity
l4_steps.kpi: Detractor case creation latency ≤ 4 hours from survey submission; 100% of NPS 0–3 cases created same day
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics-to-Salesforce webhook integration requires stable API keys and payload schema alignment; schema drift after Qualtrics XM or Salesforce release upgrades has caused dropped detractor cases in production

l4_steps.name: Correlate NPS scores with operational performance data
l4_steps.input: NPS dataset from AWS S3 joined with OTP, delay codes, load factor from Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.output: Correlation matrix: NPS vs. OTP, delay duration, cabin load, crew staffing
l4_steps.kpi: Correlation analysis refresh cycle ≤ 24 hours; cover ≥ 90% of surveyed flights with ops data join
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa operational data (delay codes, actual arrival times) and Qualtrics survey responses use different flight key structures (Altéa uses PNR/flight leg ID; Qualtrics uses survey metadata); cross-system join requires a maintained flight key mapping table that breaks on schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Identify systemic failure drivers and escalate
l4_steps.input: Correlation matrix and themed verbatim clusters from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Systemic issue flags (e.g. route-level catering failure, recurring IFE outage) with owning department assignment
l4_steps.kpi: Systemic issues identified within 48 hours of NPS batch; ≥ 80% of flags routed to correct owning department
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-functional escalation path for systemic NPS drivers (e.g. catering contracted to LSG Sky Chefs, IFE operated by Panasonic Avionics) lacks SLA enforcement; owning department may dispute root cause assignment without corroborating ops data

l4_steps.name: Generate NPS insight report for leadership
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, segment data, systemic flags, and verbatim themes
l4_steps.output: Weekly NPS insight report: route heatmap, driver waterfall, trend vs. prior period
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by Monday 08:00 local time for prior week's flights; ≥ 95% data completeness
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual Tableau report assembly from multiple AWS Redshift views causes inconsistent metric definitions across business units; finance uses different on-time threshold (D15) vs. CX team (D0), creating conflicting NPS driver narratives

l4_steps.name: Prioritise detractor outreach by severity tier
l4_steps.input: Detractor case queue from Salesforce Service Cloud prioritised by NPS score and LTV flag
l4_steps.output: Prioritised outreach list: Tier 1 (NPS 0–3, high-value loyalty member), Tier 2 (NPS 4–6)
l4_steps.kpi: Tier 1 first contact attempt within 24 hours; Tier 2 within 72 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce Service Cloud LTV flag relies on Amadeus Altéa loyalty tier sync; sync runs nightly so recently tier-upgraded passengers are misclassified as standard for up to 24 hours, delaying priority recovery for high-value detractors

l4_steps.name: Execute personalised recovery — miles or voucher
l4_steps.input: Detractor case with verified passenger loyalty profile and verbatim complaint theme
l4_steps.output: Recovery action logged: goodwill miles credited via Altéa loyalty API or travel voucher issued
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery offer acceptance rate ≥ 65%; average goodwill cost per case ≤ $35 equivalent
l4_steps.pain_point: Goodwill miles crediting via Altéa loyalty API requires PNR match; passengers who booked via OTA without loyalty number attached cannot receive miles recovery without manual agent intervention, increasing handle time by 12–15 minutes per case

l4_steps.name: Confirm recovery satisfaction and close case
l4_steps.input: Recovery action confirmation and passenger acknowledgement
l4_steps.output: Case closed with recovery outcome tag; re-survey flag set if unresolved
l4_steps.kpi: Case resolution rate ≥ 80% within 7 days; re-escalation rate ≤ 5%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated post-recovery satisfaction check; agents manually follow up by phone or email with no structured close-loop survey, making it impossible to measure whether recovery actions actually reversed detractor sentiment

l4_steps.name: Publish NPS dashboard to operational stakeholders
l4_steps.input: Aggregated NPS scores, driver analysis, recovery metrics from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Live Tableau dashboard: route NPS heatmap, weekly trend, detractor volume, recovery SLA status
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency ≤ 4 hours; ≥ 200 active monthly dashboard users across CX, Ops, and Commercial
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server licence costs scale with named users; CX team frequently requests ad-hoc access for seasonal staff or agency partners which requires IT procurement cycle of 5–10 business days, delaying insight access during high-disruption periods

l4_steps.name: Update CX improvement backlog with NPS-driven initiatives
l4_steps.input: Systemic failure flags, driver waterfall, and benchmarked NPS gap vs. target
l4_steps.output: Prioritised improvement backlog items linked to specific NPS driver themes and owning teams
l4_steps.kpi: ≥ 3 backlog items added per monthly NPS review cycle; ≥ 60% of prior-cycle items in active delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: NPS-driven improvement initiatives require cross-functional commitment from Ops, IT, and Commercial; without formal governance linking NPS driver escalation to change request prioritisation, improvement backlog items stall at department boundaries
